The archive is sparse and strongly concentrated at order 3: seven order-3 cells are filled, compared with three at order 2, one at order 4, and none in the searchable order-1 grid. Within order 3, held-out error generally improves as stage count and bucket increase, reaching 2.647e-02 at six stages in bucket 4. That cell also has the lowest recorded search error, 6.697e-03. The current cell is therefore aligned with the most favorable observed region, although most neighboring buckets remain unexplored.

The pattern is consistent with additional stages providing more freedom to satisfy order conditions while accommodating fixed-point coefficient constraints. The progression from three-stage buckets 2, 3 through six-stage bucket 4 also suggests that higher buckets may become accessible only after enough stages are available. Order alone does not explain performance: the sole order-4 entry has a held-out error of 7.851e-02, worse than every archived order-3 entry, so coefficient quality, quantization effects, and search convergence appear at least as relevant as formal order in the tested regime.

A substantial gap between search and held-out error appears throughout the archive. For example, the six-stage order-3 candidate rises from 6.697e-03 in search to 2.647e-02 when held out, while the four-stage order-2 candidate rises from 1.739e-02 to 8.301e-02. This could reflect optimization toward the search cases, sensitivity to the held-out problem distribution, or numerical effects that are not captured by the search objective. The supplied material contains no literature-digest text, so direct agreement with particular published constructions cannot be assessed; the broad tradeoff among order conditions, stage count, coefficient restrictions, and generalization is nevertheless the natural literature context for these observations.

No hypotheses are currently open or refuted, and the large number of empty cells makes boundary claims premature. The next useful examination is the local neighborhood around order 3 at five and six stages, especially buckets 3, 5, with repeated evaluations to determine whether the apparent improvement is stable. It would also be useful to populate comparable order-2 and order-4 cells, inspect per-problem held-out failures, and test whether the search-to-held-out gap persists under broader or differently weighted search cases.
